name: Parachute Tricuspid Valve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Parachute Tricuspid Valve

criteria.description: Presence of a single papillary muscle supporting all tricuspid valve leaflets
Restricted mobility of tricuspid valve leaflets leading to stenosis or regurgitation
Echocardiographic visualization of parachute morphology of the tricuspid valve apparatus
Presence of associated congenital heart defects (e.g., atrial septal defect)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a single papillary muscle supporting all tricuspid valve leaflets with echocardiographic confirmation of restricted leaflet mobility
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings; cardiac MRI may be used for further anatomical assessment.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tricuspid valve leaflet tethering with single papillary muscle
searchTerms: tricuspid valve leaflet pulled by single muscle

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tricuspid valve stenosis due to restricted leaflet motion

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output
enlarged liver from right heart failure
right-sided heart failure causing liver enlargement
blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

rare.symptomName: Ascites secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from heart failure
ascites caused by right heart failure

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes secondary to congestive hepatopathy
BNP elevation indicating right heart strain
imaging: Echocardiography showing single papillary muscle and restricted tricuspid valve leaflets
Cardiac MRI confirming parachute morphology and associated anomalies
Right atrial enlargement on chest X-ray
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with congenital heart disease syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement and possible arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Valve leaflet thickening without parachute morphology
Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets

redFlags: Severe tricuspid stenosis causing right heart failure
references: Anderson RH, et al. The anatomy of the parachute tricuspid valve. Cardiol Young. 2015;25(3):456-462.
